svg.desc: Four molecular routes lead to different readouts. A floor-plate cue enables local ROBO3.2 production and translation-coupled RNA decay. RBM20 regulates titin spring exon exclusion and thereby changes spring length. Including the Tra2b poison exon reduces productive output. Loss of that exon disrupts meiotic prophase. Astrocytes release soluble DLK1 by cleavage. A neural stem cell requires its own membrane-bound form to respond to soluble DLK1 by forming more neurospheres.

g.text: Axon guidance · translation at the floor plate
UPF2 loss increases postcrossing ROBO3.2 protein in axons.
Cardiac mechanics · RBM20 represses titin spring exons
Fetal rat cardiomyocytes with longer titin develop less passive tension.
Germ-cell splicing · poison-exon inclusion limits TRA2B dosage
Poison-exon deletion disrupts meiotic prophase in mouse germ cells.
Neural stem-cell niche · two cells supply different DLK1 forms
Restoring the appropriate form in each cell type rescues the response.
